name: English Tenses in Use
description: Use all twelve English tense-aspect forms in practical present, past, and future situations.

cards.front: Mia has the same Monday task every week. Complete the sentence: Mia ___ the sales report before lunch every Monday.
cards.answer: Mia sends the sales report before lunch every Monday.
cards.explanation: Use the present simple for a repeated routine. The third-person singular subject “Mia” takes “sends.”
cards.example: Jon checks the inventory every Friday.
options: Mia sends the sales report before lunch every Monday.
Mia is sending the sales report before lunch every Monday.

cards.front: You are composing an email at this moment. Complete the sentence: I ___ an email to the landlord right now.
cards.answer: I am writing an email to the landlord right now.
cards.explanation: Use the present continuous for an action in progress at the moment of speaking.
cards.example: I am waiting for the bus right now.
options: I write an email to the landlord right now.
I am writing an email to the landlord right now.

cards.front: Their apartment is being repaired, so this arrangement lasts only two weeks. Complete: They ___ with friends for two weeks.
cards.answer: They are staying with friends for two weeks.
cards.explanation: Use the present continuous for a temporary situation around the present time.
cards.example: Ravi is working from the library while his internet is down.
options: They stay with friends for two weeks.
They are staying with friends for two weeks.

cards.front: According to the printed timetable, the last train departs at 10:15 tonight. Complete: The last train ___ at 10:15 tonight.
cards.answer: The last train leaves at 10:15 tonight.
cards.explanation: Use the present simple for a fixed timetable, even when it refers to the future.
cards.example: The museum opens at nine tomorrow morning.
options: The last train leaves at 10:15 tonight.
The last train is leaving at 10:15 tonight.

cards.front: You and Priya already arranged a lunch for Friday. Complete: Priya and I ___ for lunch on Friday.
cards.answer: Priya and I are meeting for lunch on Friday.
cards.explanation: Use the present continuous for a personal future arrangement that has already been made.
cards.example: We are visiting the new office next Tuesday.
options: Priya and I meet for lunch on Friday.
Priya and I are meeting for lunch on Friday.

cards.front: You have no information about the answer. Complete: I ___ the answer.
cards.answer: I do not know the answer.
cards.explanation: “Know” describes a state, so it normally uses the present simple rather than the continuous form.
cards.example: Sam understands the instructions now.
options: I do not know the answer.
I am not knowing the answer.

cards.front: Ask about the regular frequency of Leo’s gym visits. Complete the question: How often ___ to the gym?
cards.answer: How often does Leo go to the gym?
cards.explanation: Use “does” plus the base verb to ask about the frequency of a third-person routine.
cards.example: How often does your team meet in person?
options: How often does Leo go to the gym?
How often is Leo going to the gym?

cards.front: The printer is idle at this moment. Complete: No one ___ the printer right now.
cards.answer: No one is using the printer right now.
cards.explanation: Use the present continuous to describe what is or is not happening now.
cards.example: The children are not watching television at the moment.
options: No one uses the printer right now.
No one is using the printer right now.

cards.front: Teaching mathematics is Maya’s permanent job. Complete: Maya ___ mathematics at a secondary school.
cards.answer: Maya teaches mathematics at a secondary school.
cards.explanation: Use the present simple for a stable job or long-term situation.
cards.example: My neighbor manages a small grocery store.
options: Maya teaches mathematics at a secondary school.
Maya is teaching mathematics at a secondary school.

cards.front: The number of people using the service is gradually increasing. Use the present continuous to emphasize this developing trend: More people ___ the service each month.
cards.answer: More people are using the service each month.
cards.explanation: Use the present continuous for a changing trend that is developing around the present.
cards.example: Winters are becoming warmer in this region.
options: More people use the service each month.
More people are using the service each month.

cards.front: Describe both a usual commute and this week’s temporary change: I usually ___ the bus, but this week I ___ to work.
cards.answer: I usually take the bus, but this week I am cycling to work.
cards.explanation: The present simple describes the usual commute; the present continuous describes the temporary change this week.
cards.example: Nina normally cooks at home, but this week she is eating at the office café.
options: I usually take the bus, but this week I am cycling to work.
I am usually taking the bus, but this week I cycle to work.

cards.front: State the scientific fact using the correct present tense: Water ___ at 100°C at sea level.
cards.answer: Water boils at 100°C at sea level.
cards.explanation: Use the present simple for a general scientific fact.
cards.example: Ice melts when its temperature rises above 0°C.
options: Water boils at 100°C at sea level.
Water is boiling at 100°C at sea level.

cards.front: A colleague is editing a document now. Ask about that current task: What ___ on?
cards.answer: What are you working on?
cards.explanation: Use the present continuous in a question about an action happening now.
cards.example: Why are you looking at the schedule?
options: What do you work on?
What are you working on?

cards.front: The usual manager is away, and Ana has this responsibility only this week. Complete: Ana ___ the morning meeting this week.
cards.answer: Ana is leading the morning meeting this week.
cards.explanation: Use the present continuous for a temporary responsibility during a limited period.
cards.example: I am covering the front desk until Friday.
options: Ana leads the morning meeting this week.
Ana is leading the morning meeting this week.

cards.front: Nora normally drives, but her car is at the garage today. Complete both parts: Nora usually ___ to work, but today she ___ the train.
cards.answer: Nora usually drives to work, but today she is taking the train.
cards.explanation: Use the present simple for Nora’s normal habit and the present continuous for today’s temporary action.
cards.example: We usually eat indoors, but today we are sitting outside.
options: Nora usually drives to work, but today she is taking the train.
Nora is usually driving to work, but today she takes the train.

cards.front: You hear repeated knocks at the door at this moment. Complete: Listen! Someone ___ at the door.
cards.answer: Listen! Someone is knocking at the door.
cards.explanation: “Listen!” directs attention to an action happening now, so use the present continuous.
cards.example: Look! A cyclist is crossing the bridge.
options: Listen! Someone knocks at the door.
Listen! Someone is knocking at the door.

cards.front: The shop’s regular schedule says it is closed every Sunday. Complete: The shop ___ on Sundays.
cards.answer: The shop does not open on Sundays.
cards.explanation: Use the present simple negative for a regular schedule, with “does not” plus the base verb.
cards.example: The clinic does not accept walk-ins on weekends.
options: The shop does not open on Sundays.
The shop is not opening on Sundays.

cards.front: Your friend has a heavy coat on now, although the room is warm. Ask about the current choice: Why ___ a coat?
cards.answer: Why are you wearing a coat?
cards.explanation: Use the present continuous to ask about something the person is doing at this moment.
cards.example: Why is Ella carrying two umbrellas?
options: Why do you wear a coat?
Why are you wearing a coat?

cards.front: The blue jacket is Sam’s property. Complete: This blue jacket ___ to Sam.
cards.answer: This blue jacket belongs to Sam.
cards.explanation: “Belong” describes possession, a state, so it normally uses the present simple.
cards.example: These keys belong to the building manager.
options: This blue jacket belongs to Sam.
This blue jacket is belonging to Sam.

cards.front: The café normally closes at six, but it has a special late event today. Complete both parts: The café usually ___ at six, but today it ___ open until nine.
cards.answer: The café usually closes at six, but today it is staying open until nine.
cards.explanation: Use the present simple for the normal closing time and the present continuous for today’s temporary exception.
cards.example: The library usually shuts at five, but tonight it is closing at eight.
options: The café usually closes at six, but today it is staying open until nine.
The café is usually closing at six, but today it stays open until nine.

cards.front: Mai bought the café in 2022 and still owns it. Complete: Mai ___ the café since 2022.
cards.answer: Mai has owned the café since 2022.
cards.explanation: Present perfect links a state begun in the past to now.
cards.example: We have known our neighbors for years.
options: Mai has owned the café since 2022.
Mai owned the café since 2022.
Mai has been owning the café since 2022.

cards.front: Ask about an experience at any time before now: ___ sushi?
cards.answer: Have you ever tried sushi?
cards.explanation: Ever asks about life experience up to now.
cards.example: Have you ever visited Da Nang?
options: Have you ever tried sushi?
Have you ever try sushi?
Did you try sushi tomorrow?

cards.front: Nam has paint on his hands because the activity started an hour ago and is still continuing. Complete: Nam ___ the kitchen for an hour.
cards.answer: Nam has been painting the kitchen for an hour.
cards.explanation: Present perfect continuous focuses on an activity's duration from past to now.
cards.example: I have been waiting for the bus since eight.
options: Nam has been painting the kitchen for an hour.
Nam painted the kitchen for an hour.
Nam has painted the kitchen for an hour.

cards.front: Use the present perfect continuous to explain your tiredness: I ___ since dawn.
cards.answer: I have been working since dawn.
cards.explanation: The form have been plus verb-ing shows ongoing recent activity.
cards.example: She has been studying all afternoon.
options: I have been working since dawn.
I worked since dawn.
I have worked since dawn.

cards.front: The flight landed once at 9:00 last night. Complete: The flight ___ at 9:00 last night.
cards.answer: The flight landed at 9:00 last night.
cards.explanation: Simple past describes a finished action at a specific past time.
cards.example: Our guests arrived after dinner.
options: The flight landed at 9:00 last night.
The flight has landed at 9:00 last night.
The flight was landing at 9:00 last night.

cards.front: At 9:00 last night, the action was in progress. Complete: I ___ for tomorrow's meeting at 9:00 last night.
cards.answer: I was preparing for tomorrow's meeting at 9:00 last night.
cards.explanation: Past continuous describes an action in progress at a past time.
cards.example: They were driving home when it began to rain.
options: I was preparing for tomorrow's meeting at 9:00 last night.
I prepared for tomorrow's meeting at 9:00 last night.
I had prepared for tomorrow's meeting at 9:00 last night.

cards.front: Use the past perfect to show that the server restart happened before the update began: The server ___ before the update began.
cards.answer: The server had restarted before the update began.
cards.explanation: Past perfect marks the earlier of two stated past actions.
cards.example: The meeting had ended before I arrived.
options: The server had restarted before the update began.
The server restarted before the update began.
The server was restarting before the update began.

cards.front: Use past perfect continuous for the duration before the meeting: The team ___ the proposal for an hour before the meeting began.
cards.answer: The team had been discussing the proposal for an hour before the meeting began.
cards.explanation: Past perfect continuous shows duration leading up to a past point.
cards.example: She had been driving for two hours when she stopped.
options: The team had been discussing the proposal for an hour before the meeting began.
The team was discussing the proposal for an hour before the meeting began.
The team had discussed the proposal for an hour before the meeting began.

cards.front: Make a prediction based on your opinion: I think the new feature ___ popular.
cards.answer: I think the new feature will be popular.
cards.explanation: Will expresses a prediction.
cards.example: I think the weather will improve tomorrow.
options: I think the new feature will be popular.
I think the new feature is being popular.
I think the new feature will being popular.

cards.front: At 3:00 tomorrow, the appointment will be in progress. Complete: At 3:00 tomorrow, I ___ with the client.
cards.answer: At 3:00 tomorrow, I will be meeting with the client.
cards.explanation: Future continuous describes an action in progress at a specified future time.
cards.example: This time next week, we will be travelling.
options: At 3:00 tomorrow, I will be meeting with the client.
At 3:00 tomorrow, I will meet with the client.
At 3:00 tomorrow, I will have met with the client.

cards.front: Use the future perfect for a task completed before Friday: By Friday, Elena ___ the report.
cards.answer: By Friday, Elena will have finished the report.
cards.explanation: Future perfect shows completion before a future deadline.
cards.example: By noon, I will have sent the invoices.
options: By Friday, Elena will have finished the report.
By Friday, Elena will finish the report.
By Friday, Elena will have been finishing the report.

cards.front: Use future perfect continuous for Sam's ongoing employment: By July, Sam ___ here for five years.
cards.answer: By July, Sam will have been working here for five years.
cards.explanation: Future perfect continuous shows a duration continuing up to a future time.
cards.example: In December, they will have been living there for a decade.
options: By July, Sam will have been working here for five years.
By July, Sam will work here for five years.
By July, Sam will have worked here for five years.

cards.front: Choose the pair that reports a completed action yesterday and an unfinished result now: I ___ the invoice yesterday, but I ___ the receipt yet.
cards.answer: I sent the invoice yesterday, but I have not received the receipt yet.
cards.explanation: The dated action takes simple past while yet connects the missing receipt to now.
cards.example: We booked the room last week, but we have not received confirmation yet.
options: I sent the invoice yesterday, but I have not received the receipt yet.
I have sent the invoice yesterday, but I did not receive the receipt yet.
I was sending the invoice yesterday, but I have not received the receipt yet.

cards.front: Emphasize the ongoing activity, not its finished result: Leo ___ the proposal since 8:00 a.m., so he needs a break.
cards.answer: Leo has been writing the proposal since 8:00 a.m., so he needs a break.
cards.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes activity and duration.
cards.example: They have been testing the app all morning.
options: Leo has been writing the proposal since 8:00 a.m., so he needs a break.
Leo has written the proposal since 8:00 a.m., so he needs a break.
Leo wrote the proposal since 8:00 a.m., so he needs a break.

cards.front: One action interrupted another. Complete: While I ___ to the office, a cyclist ___ a bag.
cards.answer: While I was walking to the office, a cyclist dropped a bag.
cards.explanation: Past continuous supplies the background action and simple past supplies the completed interrupting event.
cards.example: While we were eating, the lights went out.
options: While I was walking to the office, a cyclist dropped a bag.
While I walked to the office, a cyclist was dropping a bag.
While I had walked to the office, a cyclist dropped a bag.

cards.front: Use past perfect to make the sequence explicit: First the server restarted; then the update began. Complete: The server ___ before the update began.
cards.answer: The server had restarted before the update began.
cards.explanation: The past perfect makes the earlier action explicit.
cards.example: I had saved the file before the laptop shut down.
options: The server had restarted before the update began.
The server was restarting before the update began.
The server has restarted before the update began.

cards.front: Emphasize the length of the activity before the past event: The team ___ for an hour when the manager arrived.
cards.answer: The team had been discussing the plan for an hour when the manager arrived.
cards.explanation: Past perfect continuous focuses on duration before a past event.
cards.example: We had been waiting for thirty minutes when the bus came.
options: The team had been discussing the plan for an hour when the manager arrived.
The team discussed the plan for an hour when the manager arrived.
The team was discussing the plan for an hour when the manager arrived.

cards.front: At this exact time tomorrow, the flight will be in progress. Complete: This time tomorrow, we ___ to Singapore.
cards.answer: This time tomorrow, we will be flying to Singapore.
cards.explanation: Future continuous describes an in-progress action at a future time.
cards.example: At noon, I will be presenting the budget.
options: This time tomorrow, we will be flying to Singapore.
This time tomorrow, we will fly to Singapore.
This time tomorrow, we will have flown to Singapore.

cards.front: The tickets are already booked. Use present continuous for the fixed arrangement: We ___ at the Riverside Hotel on Friday.
cards.answer: We are staying at the Riverside Hotel on Friday.
cards.explanation: Present continuous can express an arranged personal future plan.
cards.example: I am meeting the designer tomorrow morning.
options: We are staying at the Riverside Hotel on Friday.
We will be staying at the Riverside Hotel on Friday.
We have stayed at the Riverside Hotel on Friday.

cards.front: Use future perfect continuous to focus on duration up to a deadline: By next December, Priya ___ for this company for ten years.
cards.answer: By next December, Priya will have been working for this company for ten years.
cards.explanation: Future perfect continuous emphasizes duration, unlike future perfect's completed result.
cards.example: By 2030, I will have been teaching for fifteen years.
options: By next December, Priya will have been working for this company for ten years.
By next December, Priya will have worked for this company for ten years.
By next December, Priya will be working for this company for ten years.

cards.front: Correct the tense error: “I have met her at the workshop yesterday.”
cards.answer: I met her at the workshop yesterday.
cards.explanation: A finished event with yesterday requires simple past.
cards.example: We signed the contract last Monday.
options: I met her at the workshop yesterday.
I have met her at the workshop yesterday.
I was meeting her at the workshop yesterday.

cards.front: Correct the tense error. The action was in progress at 8:00 last night: “At 8:00 last night, I prepared dinner.”
cards.answer: At 8:00 last night, I was preparing dinner.
cards.explanation: An action in progress at a specific past time uses past continuous.
cards.example: At noon, they were discussing the schedule.
options: At 8:00 last night, I was preparing dinner.
At 8:00 last night, I prepared dinner.
At 8:00 last night, I had prepared dinner.

cards.front: Correct the tense error: “By the deadline on Friday, we will finish the report.”
cards.answer: By the deadline on Friday, we will have finished the report.
cards.explanation: Future perfect marks completion before a deadline.
cards.example: By tomorrow, I will have completed the form.
options: By the deadline on Friday, we will have finished the report.
By the deadline on Friday, we will finish the report.
By the deadline on Friday, we will have been finishing the report.

cards.front: Correct the tense error using future perfect continuous: “By June, Sam will work here for five years.”
cards.answer: By June, Sam will have been working here for five years.
cards.explanation: Future perfect continuous shows the duration up to June.
cards.example: By August, we will have been renting this office for a year.
options: By June, Sam will have been working here for five years.
By June, Sam will work here for five years.
By June, Sam will have worked here for five years.

cards.front: Use present perfect to complete the unfinished-result sentence: I ___ (not / receive) a reply yet.
cards.answer: I have not received a reply yet.
cards.explanation: Yet with an unfinished result calls for present perfect.
cards.example: She has not called me yet.

cards.front: Use past perfect to complete: The taxi ___ (leave) before we reached the hotel.
cards.answer: The taxi had left before we reached the hotel.
cards.explanation: Past perfect marks the earlier past action.
cards.example: The store had closed before we arrived.

cards.front: Use future continuous to complete: At 10:00 on Tuesday, I ___ (present) the budget.
cards.answer: At 10:00 on Tuesday, I will be presenting the budget.
cards.explanation: Future continuous describes an action in progress at a future time.
cards.example: At six, they will be having dinner.

cards.front: Use future simple to make an offer: I ___ (carry) your bag.
cards.answer: I will carry your bag.
cards.explanation: Future simple with will can make an immediate offer.
cards.example: I will call a taxi for you.
